# fjordrun_service_environment (Resource)

A service's settings in an additional environment, for example a different branch and fewer replicas in staging. Services exist in every environment of their project, so nothing is created: this resource takes over the service's instance in `environment_id` and applies what you set; what you leave out keeps its current value. Use it for every environment except the one `fjordrun_service` manages (`fjordrun_service.environment_id`): two resources managing the same environment fight each other.

The API can't reset an instance to the service's defaults, so destroying this resource leaves the settings as they are. `on_destroy` decides what happens to the running service.

Functions have their own resource: `fjordrun_function_environment`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "team_id" {
  type = string
}

resource "fjordrun_project" "shop" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "shop"
}

resource "fjordrun_environment" "staging" {
  project_id = fjordrun_project.shop.id
  name       = "staging"
}

resource "fjordrun_service" "web" {
  project_id     = fjordrun_project.shop.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_project.shop.default_environment_id
  name           = "web"
  source         = { type = "github", repo = "acme/shop", branch = "main" }
  deploy         = { replicas = 3 }

  # the staging instance is created by the service: it must exist first
  depends_on = [fjordrun_environment.staging]
}

# The same service in staging: another branch, one small replica.
resource "fjordrun_service_environment" "web_staging" {
  service_id     = fjordrun_service.web.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_environment.staging.id

  source    = { type = "github", repo = "acme/shop", branch = "develop" }
  deploy    = { replicas = 1 }
  resources = { memory_mb = 512 }
}

# Pair with auto_deploy = false on the provider or the service, or a change deploys twice.
resource "fjordrun_deployment" "web_staging" {
  service_id     = fjordrun_service_environment.web_staging.service_id
  environment_id = fjordrun_service_environment.web_staging.environment_id
  triggers       = { config = fjordrun_service_environment.web_staging.config_hash }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment ID.
- `service_id` (String) Service ID.

### Optional

- `auto_deploy` (Boolean) Deploy when this resource is created or changes. Leave out to use the provider's `auto_deploy` (default `true`). With `false` the change is saved and goes live with the next deployment, which `fjordrun_deployment` makes explicit.
- `billing_granularity` (String) Billing granularity: `second`, `minute` or `hour`.
- `build` (Attributes) How the image is built (GitHub sources). Fields you leave out keep the value the API has. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--build))
- `deploy` (Attributes) How the service runs. Fields you leave out keep the value the API has (its default for the service's kind, at first). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--deploy))
- `on_destroy` (String) What destroying this resource does to the service in this environment: `stop` (default) removes its active deployment, so it stops running and billing; `keep` leaves it running.
- `resources` (Attributes) CPU and memory limits. Your plan's limits apply. Fields you leave out keep the value the API has. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resources))
- `source` (Attributes) Where the code or image comes from. Leave out for an empty service. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--source))

### Read-Only

- `config_hash` (String) Digest of the source and configuration in this environment as the API holds them. Use it as a `fjordrun_deployment` trigger.
- `id` (String) `service_id/environment_id`.
- `private_hostname` (String) Hostname reachable from the other services of the environment.
- `private_hostnames` (List of String) The short hostname, then the project-qualified one.
- `status` (String) Status in this environment.

<a id="nestedatt--build"></a>
### Nested Schema for `build`

Optional:

- `build_command` (String) Build command. An empty string clears it.
- `builder` (String) `auto` (repository Dockerfile, else detection, else Nixpacks), `nixpacks` or `dockerfile`.
- `dockerfile_path` (String) Path of the Dockerfile. An empty string clears it.
- `watch_paths` (List of String) Only pushes touching these paths deploy (up to 50).


<a id="nestedatt--deploy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `deploy`

Optional:

- `cron_schedule` (String) Cron expression (kind `cron`). An empty string clears it.
- `healthcheck_path` (String) HTTP path of the health check, starting with `/`. An empty string turns the check off.
- `healthcheck_timeout` (Number) Seconds a new deployment has to become healthy (10-3600).
- `max_restarts` (Number) Restarts allowed before the deployment counts as crashed (0-100).
- `port` (Number) Port the service listens on (1-65535).
- `replicas` (Number) Number of replicas (0-50; your plan's limit applies). 0 stops the service.
- `restart_policy` (String) `on_failure`, `always` or `never`.
- `sleep_after_minutes` (Number) Minutes without requests before sleeping (1-1440).
- `sleep_when_idle` (Boolean) Scale to zero after a while without requests, and wake on the next one.
- `start_command` (String) Command to start the service. An empty string clears it.


<a id="nestedatt--resources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resources`

Optional:

- `cpu_millicores` (Number) CPU limit in millicores (100-64000).
- `memory_mb` (Number) Memory limit in MB (128-131072).


<a id="nestedatt--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `source`

Optional:

- `branch` (String) Branch to build (type `github`). Leave out for the repository's default branch.
- `image` (String) Container image reference (type `image`).
- `repo` (String) `owner/name` of the GitHub repository (type `github`).
- `root_dir` (String) Directory in the repository to build from (type `github`).
- `type` (String) Required when `source` is set: `github`, `image` or `empty`. `template` only describes a service adopted from a template.

Read-Only:

- `template` (String) The template the service came from, if any.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# service_id/environment_id
terraform import fjordrun_service_environment.web_staging 77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777/88888888-8888-8888-8888-888888888888
```
